methods.label: Reveal two simpler power relationships
methods.explanation:
Comparing the given exponents helps express \(y\) in terms of \(x\). Because \(t>0\) and \(t\ne1\), all the exponents are defined and both \(x\) and \(y\) are positive. Thus positive-base real-power laws apply:
\[
y=t^{t/(t-1)}
=\left(t^{1/(t-1)}\right)^t=x^t.
\]
Dividing the original expressions also gives
\[
\frac{y}{x}
=t^{\frac{t}{t-1}-\frac{1}{t-1}}
=t^{\frac{t-1}{t-1}}=t,
\]
so \(y=tx\). Combining these two relationships,
\[
y^x=(x^t)^x=x^{tx}=x^y.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{y^x=x^y}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\), holds throughout the stated domain.
methods.levelReason: Positive-base real exponent laws and simple fraction simplification suffice; logarithms are unnecessary.
